prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a rear-end collision in Pasadena, Texas, and has neck strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1415; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'd rather not give my name on a recording, but I understand the process. You can refer to me as the claimant.

Q: That's fine. Can you tell me where you were when the collision occurred?

A: I was stopped at a red light on a main road in Pasadena, Texas, waiting to turn left.

Q: What happened next?

A: The car behind me didn't stop in time. I felt a hard jolt from behind, and my head snapped back and then forward.

Q: Did you see the other vehicle before impact?

A: Only in the rearview mirror, a second before. I didn't have time to react.

Q: Were you able to drive your vehicle from the scene?

A: Yes, but the bumper was damaged and I was pretty shaken up. I pulled into a parking lot and waited for the police.

Q: Did you seek medical attention?

A: I went to an urgent care clinic that afternoon. They diagnosed me with a neck strain and gave me a muscle relaxant and a referral to a physical therapist.

Q: How are you feeling now?

A: My neck is stiff, especially in the morning, and I get headaches when I'm sitting at my desk for long periods. Turning my head to check blind spots is painful.

Q: Have you missed any work because of the injury?

A: I missed two days and I'm on limited duties for another week. My supervisor has been understanding about it.

Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?

A: Only that I was following all the traffic rules and I'm committed to getting better. I'd appreciate a prompt response on the claim.

Q: Thank you. This concludes the recorded statement.
